payload.blocks: §7 task list of ds-h3fvnp6qbt (head communication); the mailbox-in-cage, rotation and refusal fixes go on without it
payload.headline: Who walks the channel ladder: each head by itself, or one send door that tries the channels in order?

parts.cause: The owner's diagnosis: a channel always exists but the sending head lacks the capability to use all of it. Tonight Miu stopped after two failures although two other channels worked.

options.cost: One phase more than the fixes alone.
options.does: The head sends once; the door checks availability from live facts, tries the rungs fastest first and answers which rung delivered or why none did.
options.gain: Deterministic: no head can skip a rung or give up early; the skill shrinks to 'send, read the answer'.
options.harm: The send door grows a fallback step that spans the mailbox and the Event Store.
options.label: One send door walks the ladder

options.cost: Smallest: one shared file and refusal text.
options.does: A shared skill file teaches the ladder; every refusal names the next rung; the head tries the next rung itself.
options.gain: No new logic in the send path.
options.harm: Depends on each model following the skill under pressure, which is exactly what failed tonight.
options.label: Each head walks it, taught

parts.recommendation: One send door walks the ladder; the shared skill file and the refusal text stay as the explanation, not as the mechanism.

scope.allows: Choosing who walks the ladder for ds-h3fvnp6qbt.
scope.forbids: Widening any persona's grants, adding a channel beyond the three named rungs, or changing the owner-side wording (ds-cfsfcbknl6).

parts.what: Owner principle (2026-11-25): use the fastest available channel first, then step down. The ladder is: mailbox (same machine, recipient live), then a supervision event on the Event Store (crosses machines), then the owner question store. Someone has to try the rungs in order for each message.
